abstract: A 3.8 kg female baby, who was born on 7-2-92 by normal vaginal delivery at a zonal hospital in the Southern Highlands of Tanzania, was initially noted to have had an "ectopic" anus (an ano-perineal fistula) but was otherwise normal. She had delay in the passage of meconium upto the third day, and by the fifth day had developed marked abdominal distension. Following a period of unsuccessful saline "enemas" she had to undergo a right transverse colostomy in the fourth week (which relieved the distension) for what was then presumed to be Hirschsprung's Disease. She was referred to the National Referral hospital in Dar es Salaam a year later, where she was found to have an entirely intra-pelvic sacrococcygeal teratoma in association with a "low" anorectal malformation. This unusual case is of interest because of the rare association of intrapelvic sacrococcygeal teratoma with anorectal malformation which led to the initial mis-diagnosis of hirschsprung's disease.
abstract_ja: 1992年2月7日にタンザニア南部高地の地方病院で正常経膣分娩により出生した、体重3.8kgの女児。肛門が異所性（肛門会陰瘻）として認められたが、それ以外は正常であった。出生後3日目まで胎便排出が遅延し、5日目までに著明な腹部膨満が出現した。生理食塩水による浣腸が効果を示さなかったため、生後4週で右横行結腸人工肛門造設術を受けた（膨満は軽快）。当時ヒルシュスプルング病と推定されたためである。1年後、国立紹介病院（ダルエスサラーム）を受診し、低位の肛門直腸奇形を伴う完全骨盤内仙尾部奇形腫が認められた。骨盤内仙尾部奇形腫と肛門直腸奇形の合併はまれであり、ヒルシュスプルング病との初期誤診につながったため、本症例は興味深い。
